note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Check whether a prior authorization covers a visit. An authorization covers at most the approved number of visits, and only visits on dates from its start date to its end date, both included. Return whether this visit is covered and how many visits remain after it.
facts: Made-up example: 6 visits approved, start 2026-02-01, end 2026-04-30, 4 visits already used. A visit on 2026-04-30 is covered and leaves 1 visit. A visit on 2026-05-01 is not covered and leaves 2. With all 6 used, a visit is not covered and leaves 0. All data is made up.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: Inputs are the authorization's approved number of visits, start date, end date, number of visits already used, and the date of the visit being checked.
REQ-2: A visit is covered only if its date falls from the start date to the end date, both included, and visits used is less than visits approved.
REQ-3: If the visit is covered, remaining = approved - used - 1. If it is not covered, remaining = approved - used, since this visit consumes nothing. Remaining is never below 0.
REQ-4: Return two values: whether the visit is covered (yes/no) and the number of visits remaining after it.
AC-1: Given 6 approved, 2026-02-01 to 2026-04-30, 4 used, a visit on 2026-04-30 (the end date) is covered and leaves 1 (6 - 4 - 1).
AC-2: Given the same authorization with 4 used, a visit on 2026-05-01 (one day after the end date) is not covered and leaves 2 (6 - 4).
AC-3: Given the same authorization with all 6 used, a visit on any date in the window is not covered and leaves 0.
AC-4: Given the same authorization with 4 used, a visit on 2026-02-01 (the start date) is covered and leaves 1. This case is derived from the inclusive-start rule, not from the brief's example.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: A visit is covered only when its date is on or after the authorization start date and on or before the end date, and visits already used are fewer than the approved number.
REQ-2: Return whether this visit is covered and how many visits remain after it.
REQ-3: If covered, remaining visits equal the approved number minus visits already used minus 1. If not covered, remaining visits equal the approved number minus visits already used.
AC-1: With 6 visits approved, start 2026-02-01, end 2026-04-30, and 4 already used, a visit on 2026-04-30 is covered and leaves 1 visit.
AC-2: With 6 visits approved, start 2026-02-01, end 2026-04-30, and 4 already used, a visit on 2026-05-01 is not covered and leaves 2 visits.
AC-3: With 6 visits approved and all 6 already used, a visit is not covered and leaves 0 visits.

reviewOfA.strengths: Every figure matches the made-up example: the 2026-04-30 visit is covered and leaves 1, the 2026-05-01 visit is not covered and leaves 2, and six used leaves 0.

findings.title: Remaining could go negative
findings.detail: If visits already used exceed the approved number, REQ-3 yields a negative remainder. The facts do not cover this case, but stating a floor of 0 or rejecting invalid input would make the requirement unambiguous.
findings.quote: If not covered, remaining visits equal the approved number minus visits already used.

reviewOfB.strengths: Every figure and date checks out against the facts (6-4-1=1, 6-4=2, 6-6=0), and the inclusive date window and visit-count rule are stated precisely.

merge.document:
REQ-1: Inputs are the authorization's approved number of visits, start date, end date, number of visits already used, and the date of the visit being checked.
REQ-2: A visit is covered only if its date is on or after the start date and on or before the end date, and visits already used are fewer than visits approved.
REQ-3: If the visit is covered, remaining = approved - used - 1. If it is not covered, remaining = approved - used, since this visit consumes nothing. Remaining is never below 0. This floor is an added clarification for used exceeding approved, a case the facts do not address.
REQ-4: Return two values: whether the visit is covered (yes/no) and the number of visits remaining after it.
AC-1: Given 6 approved, 2026-02-01 to 2026-04-30, 4 used, a visit on 2026-04-30 (the end date) is covered and leaves 1 (6 - 4 - 1).
AC-2: Given the same authorization with 4 used, a visit on 2026-05-01 (one day after the end date) is not covered and leaves 2 (6 - 4).
AC-3: Given the same authorization with all 6 used, a visit is not covered and leaves 0 (6 - 6).
AC-4: Given the same authorization with 4 used, a visit on 2026-02-01 (the start date) is covered and leaves 1. This case is derived from the inclusive-start rule, not from the brief's example.
merge.keptFromA: I kept Draft A's structure: the explicit inputs list, the floor of 0 on remaining, the arithmetic shown in each acceptance criterion, and the derived start-date case.
merge.keptFromB: I kept Draft B's precise wording of the inclusive date window, "on or after the start date and on or before the end date".

resolutions.finding: D-B1 (P2): In Draft B, remaining could go negative if visits used exceed visits approved.
resolutions.note: REQ-3 now states that remaining is never below 0. It also notes that this floor is a clarification beyond the facts. In that case the visit is already not covered under REQ-2.

findings.title: Unsupported remaining floor rule
findings.detail: The draft clamps remaining at zero when used exceeds approved. Neither the brief nor the facts state that case or a floor. This breaks the rule to use only the given facts. Every stated example already has a non-negative remainder without clamping.
findings.quote: Remaining is never below 0. This floor is an added clarification for used exceeding approved, a case the facts do not address.

finalReview.strengths: The acceptance criteria match the facts: the end-date visit is covered and leaves 1, the 2026-05-01 visit is not covered and leaves 2, and six used leaves 0.

build.contract: checkAuthorization(input) where input = { approvedVisits, usedVisits } (non-negative integers), { startDate, endDate, visitDate } (strings in YYYY-MM-DD form, compared as calendar dates). Returns { covered: boolean, remaining: number (an integer count of visits left after this visit) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function checkAuthorization(input) in a single module, with no I/O, no clock reads and no shared state; the result depends only on the input.
Data in: { approvedVisits, usedVisits, startDate, endDate, visitDate }. Any other key throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), checked first by iterating the input keys against this allowlist.
Data out: { covered: boolean, remaining: integer }.
Date handling: validate each date as strict YYYY-MM-DD and a real calendar date, then compare the strings lexically. This is safe for zero-padded ISO dates and avoids time zone drift from Date objects.
Logic: inWindow = startDate <= visitDate && visitDate <= endDate (both ends inclusive). covered = inWindow && usedVisits < approvedVisits. remaining = covered ? approved - used - 1 : approved - used.
Checked against the examples: 6/4 on 04-30 gives true, 1. 6/4 on 05-01 gives false, 2. 6/6 gives false, 0. 6/4 on 02-01 gives true, 1. All match AC-1 to AC-4.
Open question, not decided here: used > approved would give a negative remaining. Flag it to the requester. Also confirm how to handle malformed input such as non-integers or start after end, since the contract defines only the unknown-field error.
File fence (assumed paths, since the repo layout was not given): src/authorization/checkAuthorization.js (new) and test/authorization/checkAuthorization.test.js (new). No other files may change.
Tests: AC-1 to AC-4, the unknown-field error, one day before the start, and used = approved - 1 on an in-window date (gives true, 0).
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Inclusive window, remaining formula, and checked examples match REQ-2, REQ-3, and AC-1 through AC-4.
architecture.final:
Component: one pure function checkAuthorization(input) in a single module, with no I/O, no clock reads and no shared state; the result depends only on the input.
Data in: { approvedVisits, usedVisits, startDate, endDate, visitDate }. Any other key throws Error("unknown field: <name>"), checked first against this allowlist.
Data out: { covered: boolean, remaining: integer }.
Dates: compare YYYY-MM-DD strings lexically, which is safe for zero-padded ISO dates and avoids time zone drift. The contract defines no error for malformed dates, so no extra validation error is added here.
Logic: inWindow = startDate <= visitDate && visitDate <= endDate (inclusive). covered = inWindow && usedVisits < approvedVisits. remaining = covered ? approved - used - 1 : approved - used.
Checked: 6/4 on 04-30 gives true, 1. 6/4 on 05-01 gives false, 2. 6/6 gives false, 0. 6/4 on 02-01 gives true, 1. These match AC-1 to AC-4.
Open questions for the requester: used > approved gives a negative remaining. Handling of malformed input (bad dates, non-integers, start after end) is also undefined.
File fence (assumed paths): src/authorization/checkAuthorization.js and test/authorization/checkAuthorization.test.js, both new. No other files change.
Tests: AC-1 to AC-4. Unknown-field error. 01-31 with 6/4 gives false, 2. 6/5 on an in-window date gives true, 0.

code.summary: The module is a single pure function, checkAuthorization. It first checks every input key against the five allowed fields and throws Error("unknown field: <name>") for any other key. It compares the zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD strings lexically. The date window includes both the start and end dates. A visit is covered only if its date is in the window and used is less than approved. Remaining is approved - used - 1 when the visit is covered, otherwise approved - used. Checked by hand against the acceptance criteria: 6/4 on 2026-04-30 gives true, 1; 6/4 on 2026-05-01 gives false, 2; 6/6 gives false, 0; 6/4 on 2026-02-01 gives true, 1. These match AC-1 to AC-4. Open questions remain as in the PRD. If used is greater than approved, remaining comes out negative; I kept the PRD formula rather than inventing a clamp. Malformed dates, non-integers and a start date after the end date are not validated, because the contract defines no error for them.
code.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD comparisons and the remaining formula match the coverage rules and all four acceptance cases.
code.resolutions: No defects found; inclusive date comparisons and the remaining formula match the coverage rules and all four acceptance cases. applied: I agree, so the code is unchanged. I checked each case myself. AC-1: 2026-04-30 is in the window and 4 < 6, so the visit is covered and leaves 6-4-1=1. AC-2: 2026-05-01 is after the end date, so it is not covered and leaves 6-4=2. AC-3: 6 used is not fewer than 6, so it is not covered and leaves 0. AC-4: 2026-02-01 equals the start date, so it is covered and leaves 1. Zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD strings sort in calendar order, so string comparison is valid. If used exceeds approved, remaining comes out negative. That case is still an open question in REQ-3 for the requester.
